what: The heuristic precomputes a static CVRP model once: propositional loc/visited facts, depot and customer indices, numeric load/vehicles IDs, best-effort demand/capacity/max_vehicles values, and a directed travel-cost matrix built from grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operators plus a numeric travel-cost fallback. At evaluation it reads current location, load, and vehicles; builds the unvisited-customer set; applies a finite large penalty if remaining demand cannot fit in remaining fleet capacity; then computes a greedy capacitated completion cost. The greedy completion repeatedly chooses either the cheapest feasible direct visit from the current place (respecting load) or, when that is impossible, the cheapest feasible visit-via-depot if a new vehicle is available. It finally adds the return-to-depot cost from the last customer. Goal states return 0.0.
why: The representative instances are fleet-limited capacitated vehicle-routing problems with explicit pairwise travel costs and separate direct-visit and via-depot actions. A pure unvisited-count heuristic is uninformative because it ignores geography, while a sum-of-depot-distances heuristic ignores routing order, load, and vehicle transitions. Operator-based cost extraction exposes the actual metric costs without relying on fragile PNE substring parsing, and the greedy completion models the distinction between direct visits and via-depot reloads that appears throughout the examples. The resource-feasibility penalty prevents search from wasting effort in capacity/dead-end regions, while the final return-to-depot term ensures states where all customers are visited but the vehicle is not home still receive a meaningful cost estimate.
design: Operator-based travel-cost reconstruction from grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot actions
Precomputed directed distance and via-depot matrices plus sorted nearest-neighbor lists
Greedy capacitated routing simulation over unvisited customers
Resource/dead-end detection using best-effort capacity, demand, and max_vehicles with permissive defaults
complexity: Precomputation is O(n^2 log n) for sorting neighbor lists, where n is the number of places/customers. Each compute_heuristic call is worst-case O(n^2) because the greedy simulation may scan sorted neighbor lists for each remaining customer; with the target distribution of tens of customers this is very small. No task scans or full matrix rebuilds are performed during evaluation.
fallbacks: Travel costs are extracted primarily from grounded operator names using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. If some direct arcs are still missing, the code scans numeric variable names containing 'travel-cost(' and inserts those values. As a last resort, missing arcs are filled via the depot when both legs are known. If depot-to-customer or customer-to-depot costs are still missing after these steps, construction fails with a clear HeuristicBuildError. Capacity, demand, and max_vehicles are optional exact-name lookups: if any is absent, the resource term degrades permissively (capacity/max_vehicles as infinity and demands as zero) instead of failing.
known_limitations: The greedy routing completion is not a mathematically admissible or optimal estimate; it may overestimate by committing to locally cheap direct visits even when a different vehicle-reset sequence would be better.
If capacity, demand, or max_vehicles are absent in the translator, the resource-infeasibility penalty is weaker, so the heuristic depends more on the greedy routing component.
Customer-to-customer direct arcs missing from operators may be filled via the depot, which can overestimate those arc costs and may slightly distort the greedy completion on incomplete extractions.
